chapter_name: Kriya Aur Uske Bhed, Kaal, Aur Vachya (Verbs, Tense, and Voice)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will master the action words of Hindi, learn to time-travel using Tenses, and understand how to shift the focus of a sentence using Voice!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🏃 What is Kriya? (The Engine of the Sentence)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Kriya means 'Action'. Any word that shows an action being done or a state of being is a Verb. Without a verb, a sentence is like a car without an engine—it goes nowhere! 'Dhatu' is the root of the verb (like 'खा' - eat), and adding 'ना' makes it the basic verb form ('खाना' - to eat).

Some actions need an object to receive the action. If you say 'I am reading', someone can ask 'WHAT are you reading?' (A book). This is 'Sakarmak' (Transitive). But if you say 'I am sleeping', you cannot ask 'WHAT are you sleeping?' This action doesn't need an object, so it is 'Akarmak' (Intransitive).

Verbs change their clothes depending on WHEN the action happens! 'Bhootkaal' (Past Tense) is for actions already done (था/थे/थी). 'Vartamankaal' (Present Tense) is for actions happening right now (है/हैं/हूँ). 'Bhavishyatkaal' (Future Tense) is for actions that will happen later (गा/गे/गी).

Voice tells us who is controlling the verb. In 'Kartari Vachya' (Active Voice), the Subject is the hero ('राम सेब खाता है' - Ram eats an apple). In 'Karm Vachya' (Passive Voice), the Object becomes the hero ('राम द्वारा सेब खाया जाता है' - The apple is eaten by Ram).

Hindi has a unique third voice called 'Bhav Vachya'. It is usually negative and focuses entirely on the *inability* to do an action. Example: 'मुझसे चला नहीं जाता' (I am unable to walk / Walking is not done by me).

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The 'What and Whom' Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Write down 5 action verbs (like play, drink, laugh, cry, write). Ask the questions 'WHAT?' or 'WHOM?' to the verb. If you get a logical answer, label it 'Sakarmak' (Transitive). If it sounds silly, label it 'Akarmak' (Intransitive)!

quick_recap: ⭐ Kriya is a word that shows an action or a state of being.
⭐ Sakarmak verbs require an object to make sense; Akarmak verbs do not.
⭐ Kaal (Tense) has three main types: Past (Bhoot), Present (Vartaman), and Future (Bhavishyat).
⭐ Vachya (Voice) changes depending on whether the sentence focuses on the Subject, the Object, or the Emotion/Action.
